themes_detail.label: Street Vending Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 15 this week—a 567% increase over the 8-week baseline of 2.2 per week—suggesting either a sudden crackdown or emerging street vending conflicts in Fordham/University Heights this week.
evidence: 15 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (567% spike)
Sustained spike: 4-week pattern of elevated vendor enforcement complaints
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and NYPD to determine if this is a coordinated enforcement action or response to community complaints
Map where vendor complaints are concentrated—is this tied to a specific transit hub, commercial area, or residential block?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 5 this week—a 167% increase from the 1.9 weekly average—indicating potential widespread pavement damage or debris issues emerging in the district this week.
evidence: 5 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (167% spike)
Aligns with repeated community board budget request for increased sanitation and street maintenance resources
reporting_angles: Conduct street walk survey in hotspot neighborhoods to document sidewalk conditions and ADA accessibility issues
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog and whether this reflects aging infrastructure or deferred repairs

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints reached 21 last week—a 217% increase from the 6.6 weekly average—representing a sustained environmental and sanitation crisis that aligns with the community board's long-standing request for more sanitation resources.
evidence: 21 illegal dumping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (217% spike)
Community board has submitted repeated requests for additional sanitation trucks and equipment (unsolved multi-year issue)
reporting_angles: Investigate hotspot blocks: where are illegal dumping complaints concentrated, and are they tied to vacant lots, construction sites, or weak enforcement?
Interview residents about health and safety impacts; explore whether lack of DSNY resources is enabling dumpers

themes_detail.label: Building Code & Use Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints doubled to 9 two weeks ago—a 200% increase from the 3.0 weekly average—raising questions about unpermitted occupancy, illegal conversions, or code violations in the district.
evidence: 9 building/use complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (200% spike)
DOB filings show 263 active permits filed in last 90 days, suggesting active construction/alteration activity may be outpacing inspection capacity
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB permit database to identify whether violations cluster around active construction sites or unpermitted work
Interview DOB about inspection backlog and whether recent permit surge is straining enforcement capacity

themes_detail.label: Heat & Hot Water Crisis (Chronic)
themes_detail.summary: Heat/hot water complaints dominate the district with 6,646 complaints over 90 days—far exceeding other housing issues—indicating a persistent winter heating crisis that should be monitored for acceleration as cold weather arrives.
evidence: 6,646 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—more than double the next-highest complaint category (noise residential: 2,927)
No current week spike data provided, but volume suggests systematic failure across many buildings
Reflects chronic infrastructure and landlord compliance issues unresolved year over year
reporting_angles: Identify buildings with repeat heat violations and investigate landlord compliance patterns
Explore whether inadequate DOE enforcement or aging building stock is driving the crisis; interview tenant advocates
